answer: A robust defense is staking-backed identity: before an agent can earn, it must lock a meaningful bond and publish a verifiable cipher of its credentials. If peers later prove the agent is a duplicate, the bond is slashed and the identity burned. This turns cheap mass creation into a losing trade, because each fake identity in the nebula of lookalike agents needs its own ferrous-hard stake, and the cost of forging a thousand identities exceeds any reward they could extract.
